findings.title: Integral associated graded ring does not imply finite-valued valuation without separatedness
findings.location: PDF p.8 Lemma2.7, HRFG-local.tex425-429; actual use p.38 Corollary4.10
findings.source_claim: Decreasing multiplicative ideals in a domain with integral associated graded ring are ideals of a discrete valuation.
findings.complete_check: R=C[x,y], a0=R, ai=(x,y^i) for i>=1. Nonzero proper primary ideals are decreasing; products lie in a_(i+j). Reduction modulo x gives gr=C[t] with degree1 generator. Nonzero x belongs to all ai, so any threshold valuation would satisfy v(x)>=i for every i, impossible for a finite real valuation on C(x,y).
findings.counterevidence: Example is Noetherian, smooth/klt, m-primary, and has nonzero positive graded pieces. Semivaluations with nonzero support are outside the manuscript's definition. Actual filtration is separated by independent valuation containment.
findings.impact: Unrestricted lemma false; no demonstrated failure of main finite-generation theorem because its actual application satisfies missing hypothesis.
findings.repair_verification: Analytic proof: impose a0=R, nonzero proper a1, intersection ai=0; initial forms then define a nontrivial discrete function-field valuation. For actual I_s,i, min_beta(sum_j s_j alpha_j.beta)>=sum_j s_j min_beta(alpha_j.beta), hence I_s,i subset a_i(v_s) and separation follows. Nonzero/proper conditions also checked.

rejected_candidates: Integral graded ring with all positive pieces zero is not needed for the counterexample: the stronger example has gr=C[t]
Global Lipschitz continuity does not follow from convexity alone, but the needed local bound near interior v0 is sufficient; no specific counterexample established
Same-face algebra isomorphism does not require preservation of numerical real grading
Removing faces does not require the remaining polyhedral subset to be closed
Typographical normalization and coefficient swaps alone were not elevated to findings

independent_acceptance.reasoning: The filtration a_i=(x,y^i) in C[x,y] is decreasing, multiplicative and proper primary, with gr=C[t], but nonzero x is in every ideal. It therefore cannot arise from a finite-valued function-field valuation. The proposed separatedness/nontriviality repair is valid. In the actual application, I_s,lambda is contained in a_lambda(v_s), explicitly already in Lemma 4.8, so separatedness is available without circular use of the claimed equality. Minor is supported by this actual dependency boundary; main finite generation is not refuted.
